security.threat: An arbitrary valid self-signature is mistaken for an independently pinned writer.
security.control: Exact independently accepted key/name/head; strict successor CAS and revocation gates.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A hashed but impossible state is accepted as computation.
security.control: Replay exact program/input/execution identity before accepting or resuming.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A mesh topic or relay is mistaken for private storage.
security.control: Separate public signaling and payload-relay consent; explicit disclosure and no privacy claim.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: An unknown DNS write is repeated after restart or key rotation.
security.control: Strict write-ahead intent and exact read-only reconciliation; unknown journal retention.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A holder supplies modified, duplicate-index or wrong-manifest bytes.
security.control: Full domain-separated commitments and exact compatible indexed recovery.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Guest output is mistaken for trusted execution or broad host authority.
security.control: Separate VM effects, bounded mounts and explicit lifecycle/command reconciliation.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Malicious same-origin code can use retained key handles and read local data.
security.control: Source/asset inventory and origin boundary; nonextractability is not protection from active same-origin code.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A captured signed action is replayed at the same host or presented to another host.
security.control: Every action names its audience and carries a nonce; the host refuses a different audience, a seen nonce, or a time outside its window.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Browser, native, mobile and embedded runtimes canonicalize differently, so kappa labels or signatures disagree and one runtime accepts what another refuses.
security.control: uor-addr canonical form with explicit refusals (non-NFC, non-integer, ill-formed), published vectors and an independent Python implementation.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A delegate device (often embedded and physically exposed) acts outside its scope, reads private content, or administers the prism.
security.control: Scope checked on every action; a delegate never receives the private boundary and cannot bind or revoke.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A forged log presents a different genesis, so a new device or host adopts the wrong prism.
security.control: prism id is the kappa of exactly one self-signed genesis; the prism id travels out of band in the link offer and every record names it.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Guardians pool their shares to take over the prism.
security.control: Shares meet only at the threshold; guardians are other prisms or devices the person chose; a successful recovery is visible to every remaining device as revocations.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: An impostor asks guardians to release shares to the impostor device.
security.control: A guardian releases a share only re-wrapped to the requesting device after confirming the person out of band and comparing a code bound to that device; one deceived guardian is below the threshold.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A device claims hardware-held keys it does not have to obtain permissions a host reserves for such devices.
security.control: The protection field is a claim only; admitDevice accepts a hardware-requiring device only when a host-pinned verifier attests hardware protection of exactly that device signing key.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Someone who sees, photographs or relays the link QR code answers first and binds their own device to the prism.
security.control: One-time secret, expiry, single use, and a six-digit code bound to the joining device that the person confirms on both screens.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Hosts or relays correlate one person across services because the same prism id and device keys appear everywhere.
security.control: Each host sees only its own persona: a separate prism with per-device persona keys; the main prism log travels sealed between members and is never given to a host.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A peer or relay sends oversized sync messages or very large logs to exhaust memory and signature checks.
security.control: Byte and record bounds are checked before parsing and signature work; unknown records never become authority.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A relay or peer alters, reorders or injects prism log records.
security.control: Each record is signed and addressed by the kappa of its envelope; merge is order-independent set union; invalid or foreign records are ignored.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A thief holding one member device revokes every other device, or replaces the recovery device.
security.control: Recovery revocations take precedence: a device recovery revoked has no revocations that count, members cannot revoke or replace the recovery device, and recovery revokes every other device ever linked.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Script running in the prism origin (XSS, compromised dependency or static host) uses device key handles and reads the boundary keyring.
security.control: Device keys are non-extractable; a hardened device keeps only non-extractable derived boundary keys and cannot link members or set up recovery, so script can use keys only while it runs and can copy none out.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A revoked member keeps acting at a host through its persona key, or uses persona recovery keys it once saw.
security.control: Revoking a device revokes its persona keys at every host on the next sync; persona recovery keys are wrapped to the main recovery device and kept by no member.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Wraps recorded today are decrypted later by a quantum adversary.
security.control: Every wrap to a device that advertises ML-KEM-768 is hybrid ECDH plus ML-KEM; a classical wrap to such a device is refused; content keys are AES-256.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Every member device is lost, so the prism is lost.
security.control: Threshold recovery: the recovery key exists only as shares sealed to guardians; recovery binds a new device, revokes the rest, carries personas and rotates itself.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A rotation never reaches an offline member, so it cannot seal new content.
security.control: A device without the current key refuses to seal instead of sealing to the old key; a publish under the previous key delivers the rotation.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A person denies that one of their devices took an action.
security.control: Every action and administrative record is signed by a device bound in the prism log; software keys reachable by origin script remain a residual.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A non-member, a delegate, or a revoked device signs a bind to add a device under its control.
security.control: A bind counts only from a linked, unrevoked member with a valid signature for this prism; revocation wins over a concurrent bind.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A lost or stolen member device keeps reading new private content and following sync.
security.control: Revocation rotates the private boundary key, wraps it only to remaining members and moves the sync topic; stale keys are refused.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Bus relays and federation nodes read sync content or infer it from message sizes.
security.control: Sync topic is an HMAC under a derived boundary key; every message is AES-GCM sealed, bound to the prism id and padded to a power-of-two bucket; timing and network addresses remain observable.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Untrusted messages, replay or unknown effects exhaust application allowances.
security.control: Reserve each independent resource before effects; unknown outcomes stay charged.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: A relay replays or substitutes SDP/ICE and stale session callbacks.
security.control: Signed exact signaling, session/generation fencing and bounded channel flow.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Tab loss or eviction removes the only object fragments or recent trust anchor.
security.control: Explicit recovery export and origin-storage evidence; no guarantee after total information loss.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

security.threat: Loaded emulator, BIOS or guest differs from reviewed inventory.
security.control: Retained corresponding-source materials and exact local asset digests; live load-time remote integrity remains an assumption.
security.assessment: Conservative qualitative design assessment. High: directly supplied adversarial input; medium: environmental/host privilege or failure required. Impact describes possible consequence, not probability.

persistence.restore: Startup restores only a valid active existing record.
persistence.trust: Missing, malformed or revoked records never authorize automatic replacement.
persistence.failure: Origin eviction or device loss can destroy the only key.

persistence.storage: Origin IndexedDB exact name/key/digest with history
persistence.restore: Admitted successors persist by exact CAS before the live head changes; live restore is explicit.
persistence.trust: Independent exact key and recent digest acceptance is not derived from a self-signature.
persistence.failure: Storage failure preserves the previous live head; total loss requires independent recent evidence.

persistence.restore: Load the exact scoped candidate and perform read-only reconciliation.
persistence.trust: No timer takeover, blind retry or deletion of unresolved intent.
persistence.failure: An absent provider read does not prove the old mutation never occurred.

persistence.storage: Session RAM plus conditionally reachable peer fragments
persistence.restore: Automatically verify received bytes; repair only within admitted budgets and checked receipts.
persistence.trust: Different peer IDs do not prove failure-domain independence or future retention.
persistence.failure: All-byte loss cannot be repaired; local storage persistence does not make object cache durable.

persistence.storage: Session state or explicitly exported recovery bundle
persistence.restore: Every received checkpoint is replayed against its exact program/input/execution identity.
persistence.trust: Replay does not grant exclusive execution or prove arbitrary guest effects.
persistence.failure: Older execution identities are refused without explicit revalidation.

persistence.storage: Session-only checked vault and user-saved external file
persistence.restore: Verify complete bundle atomically; export strips accepted-trust status.
persistence.trust: Imported keys and anchors are supplied evidence, not trusted authority.
persistence.failure: External export is not a durability certificate; stale/conflicting imports refuse.

persistence.storage: Session-local epochs plus explicit history export
persistence.restore: Unknown effects remain charged; renewal is a deliberate new allowance.
persistence.trust: No automatic refund or epoch rollover.
persistence.failure: Browser reload is not durable preservation of the budget ledger.

persistence.storage: Retained host command handles and observed lifecycle
persistence.restore: Observe the selected old command result without dispatching it again.
persistence.trust: A timeout is an unknown outcome, not cancellation or rollback.
persistence.failure: Stop/destroy are pending until host confirmation; external effects are not reversible.
